title: Copying an icon carries the white canvas the export no longer does
goal: Draw an icon on a blank canvas, press Copy (Shift Command C) and paste it somewhere dark, and the white canvas comes with it as solid pixels. Exporting the same icon as a PNG now leaves that canvas out, so the two ways of handing an icon over disagree: the one you save is see-through and the one you paste is not.
notes: Found while finishing an-icon-exported-as-a-picture-can-come-out-with (2026-09-17). Repro of the composite that Copy puts on the clipboard: PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1 Scripts/playtest.sh /tmp/tmp-png-bg-forced.json --no-build wrote png-export-background-3-file-with-canvas.png, which is the same render EditorState.copyCompositeToClipboard uses (previewRenderer.render(document, store:), no background answer anywhere on that path), and reading its corner back gave top-left (5,5) rgba [255, 255, 255, 255]. The export path in the same walk wrote [0, 0, 0, 0]. The smallest fix is to let the copy take the same SVGExport.Background answer the sheet holds, through PhotonzDocument.drawn(with:flatImages:) (PhotonzCore) the way ExportSizer does; the open question is whether a copy should ask at all or simply always leave a flat canvas out, which is a UX call worth a decision card rather than a guess. PNG and TIFF both go on the pasteboard and both hold alpha.
acceptance: Copying an icon drawn on a blank canvas and pasting it into an app that shows transparency gives an icon with nothing behind it
Copying a screenshot or a captured screen still carries its background exactly as it does today
A walk proves the copied picture is see-through in every corner
